Loss-of-function variants in IRF6 disrupt the regulation of epithelial cell differentiation and keratinization, leading to developmental defects manifesting as popliteal webbing (autosomal dominant popliteal pterygium syndrome) and/or orofacial clefts (van der Woude syndrome 1).

falsification.text: The identification of pathogenic variants in IRF6 that consistently segregate with only one of the two diseases, and not the other, across multiple families would falsify the proposed shared mechanism. Additionally, if genetic studies demonstrate that the specific mutations causing popliteal pterygium syndrome have a distinct functional impact on IRF6 compared to those causing van der Woude syndrome 1, this would also challenge the hypothesis.
falsification.gnomad_variant: The presence of common variants (allele frequency > 1%) in the coding sequence of IRF6 in gnomAD that are known to cause either autosomal dominant popliteal pterygium syndrome or van der Woude syndrome 1.

partners.mechanism_chain: IRF6 (HGNC:6130) —DISRUPTS→ Interferon signaling pathway; IRF1 (HGNC:6129) —DISRUPTS→ Interferon signaling pathway; IRF6 (HGNC:6130) —LEADS_TO→ Ectodermal and craniofacial abnormalities (HP:0001071); Interferon signaling pathway —LEADS_TO→ Deficiency of T helper cells (HP:0005331); Deficiency of T helper cells (HP:0005331) —LEADS_TO→ Recurrent bacterial infections (HP:0002711). Mutations in IRF6 lead to haploinsufficiency, disrupting the interferon signaling pathway and causing ectodermal and craniofacial abnormalities characteristic of Popliteal Pterygium Syndrome. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in IRF1 also disrupt the interferon signaling pathway, leading to impaired immune cell function (specifically T helper cells) and recurrent infections seen in Immunodeficiency 117. The convergence point is the shared dysregulation of the interferon signaling pathway.

partners.mechanism_chain: IRF6 (HGNC:6091) —DISRUPTS→ Popliteal pterygium (HP:0001056); EGFR (HGNC:3437) —INCREASES→ MAPK signaling pathway (WP:WP526); EGFR (HGNC:3437) —INCREASES→ PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (WP:WP899); PIK3CA (HGNC:9535) —INCREASES→ PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (WP:WP899); BRAF (HGNC:1087) —INCREASES→ MAPK signaling pathway (WP:WP526); MAP3K8 (HGNC:6896) —INCREASES→ MAPK signaling pathway (WP:WP526); ERBB2 (HGNC:3436) —INCREASES→ MAPK signaling pathway (WP:WP526); ERBB2 (HGNC:3436) —INCREASES→ PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (WP:WP899); RB1 (HGNC:9820) —DISRUPTS→ Lung cancer (MONDO:0008903); MAPK signaling pathway (WP:WP526) —INCREASES→ Lung cancer (MONDO:0008903); PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (WP:WP899) —INCREASES→ Lung cancer (MONDO:0008903). Haploinsufficiency of IRF6 in autosomal dominant popliteal pterygium syndrome leads to developmental defects. In lung cancer, gain-of-function mutations in genes like EGFR, PIK3CA, BRAF, MAP3K8, and ERBB2 activate the MAPK and PI3K-Akt signaling pathways, promoting uncontrolled cell proliferation. The tumor suppressor RB1 also plays a role in preventing lung cancer progression. The convergence is on the shared signaling pathways (MAPK and PI3K-Akt) that are dysregulated in both conditions, though through different mechanisms (haploinsufficiency for IRF6 affecting development, and gain-of-function mutations in oncogenes driving cancer).

**Proposed mechanism:** IRF6 (HGNC:29317) —DISRUPTS→ Epithelial cell proliferation and differentiation (GO:0001700); Epithelial cell proliferation and differentiation (GO:0001700) —LEADS_TO→ Popliteal pterygium (HP:0004461); IFNGR2 (HGNC:5596) —DISRUPTS→ JAK-STAT signaling pathway (GO:0007242); IFNGR1 (HGNC:5595) —BINDS→ JAK-STAT signaling pathway (GO:0007242); JAK-STAT signaling pathway (GO:0007242) —LEADS_TO→ Immunodeficiency (HP:0002705); JAK-STAT signaling pathway (GO:0007242) —DECREASES→ Epithelial cell proliferation and differentiation (GO:0001700). Mutations in IRF6 lead to altered epithelial development, causing popliteal pterygium. Mutations in IFNGR2, which partners with IFNGR1 to form the interferon-gamma receptor, impair the JAK-STAT signaling pathway. This pathway is also critical for regulating epithelial cell proliferation and differentiation, thus linking the two diseases through a shared downstream pathway.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that IRF6 and IFNGR2 mutations do not converge on common downstream signaling pathways or cellular processes regulating epithelial cell function and immune cell responses. _(variant: A common pathogenic variant (AF > 0.01) in either IRF6 or IFNGR2 in the general population.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of interferon signaling in both epithelial development and immune function could lead to novel therapeutic strategies targeting common pathways for both rare developmental disorders and immunodeficiencies.
